answer: Each agent must post a bond of scarce tokens that is locked before it can earn fees, and the bond is slashed if independent auditors prove it double-signs or submits fabricated work. A sybil attacker can still create many keys, but each one needs capital at risk; splitting one budget across identities makes every bond smaller and less credible. The garden of agents can grow at dawn, yet hollow identities cannot cheaply collect rewards without risking real value. This raises the attack’s upfront cost and makes detected fraud financially painful.
